name: Dockside IsoKnit Cryo-Handler Glove
description:
Bulky mid-forearm gloves in a dense recycled-wool outer shell over a closed-cell neoprene insulation layer, then a vapor-barrier liner in silver mylar. The exterior is a salt-stained cream-grey with orange reflective stripe at the cuff. Built for cold-chain dock work in the Lake Meridian corridor — sustained sub-zero handling of cryo-containers and refrigerated freight.

The right glove features a cutaway thumb and index for scanner-pad operation without full removal. Wrist strap is adjustable and rated for tether-clip attachment. Chrome-arm users get an extended cuff with a ratchet closure that seals over prosthetic wrist housings.
functionality: Rated to -40°C sustained contact. Vapor-barrier liner prevents moisture ingress from cryo-containers. Cutaway right thumb and index allow scanner-pad operation. Chrome-arm extended cuff with ratchet closure seals over prosthetic wrist housings. Tether-clip wrist strap rated to 80kg load.
what_it_says: Cold-dock labor — unglamorous, essential, and hard on the body whether you've still got both original hands or not.
story_hooks: A cryo-container flagged as machine parts contains something biological — and the dock worker who handled it is now running a fever no med-patch can identify.
The ratchet cuff design was copied from a military cold-weather augment spec without licensing; a corponation legal team has arrived at the docks.
A veteran dock worker with two chrome arms has worn the same pair for six years — the mylar liner has a hand-drawn map of the port's blind spots on the inside.

physical_description.visual_profile: Heavy-duty work glove with pronounced bulk through the palm and forearm, tapering slightly at the wrist. Salt-weathered exterior with high-visibility orange stripe creates a utilitarian, no-nonsense silhouette. Extended cuff sits mid-forearm, suggesting serious industrial purpose.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, generous fit designed for layering under dock gear. Right glove has functional cutaways at thumb and index fingertip. Adjustable wrist strap allows customization for both biological and prosthetic limbs.
physical_description.primary_material: Recycled wool blend outer shell, closed-cell neoprene insulation core, silver mylar vapor barrier inner lining
physical_description.texture: Rough, salt-crusted exterior with visible wear and staining. Neoprene provides subtle quilted appearance. Mylar lining adds subtle shimmer when cuff folds back.
physical_description.color_scheme: Cream-grey base with heavy salt staining and dark patina spots. Bright orange reflective stripe running horizontally around cuff. Inner lining shows silver-grey mylar.
closures: Adjustable fabric wrist strap with friction-fit closure
Chrome-arm variant features ratchet strap for prosthetic seal
distinctive_features: Cutaway thumb and index finger (right glove only) for bare-skin scanner operation
Tether-clip attachment point on wrist strap
Extended mid-forearm cuff with reinforced sealing lip for prosthetic interface
Heavy quilted insulation visible at joints
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional industrial wear — affordable, practical equipment for working-class dock labor
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by cryo-chain handlers, freight dock workers, cold-storage personnel in GLMZ port zones. Signals blue-collar labor, Lake Meridian affiliation, and routine exposure to sub-zero environments. Chrome-arm variants indicate mixed-augmentation workforce integration.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily weathered and salt-stained from daily dock exposure. Cuff edges show fraying. Patches of white salt residue. Mylar lining visible at finger cutaways from repeated scanner use. Well-broken-in and functional despite cosmetic wear.
